article.title: PgBouncer 1.26.1 Fixes Three CVEs, Including a SCRAM Flaw That Lets a User Who Knows One Password Log In as Others
article.summary: PgBouncer 1.26.1, dated October 14, fixes CVE-2026-107350, CVE-2026-107349 and CVE-2026-107348 in versions up to 1.26.0, and changes how ignore_startup_parameters interacts with search_path.
article.body_markdown:
## Overview

PgBouncer 1.26.1, which the project's changelog titles "Only startup once", is dated 2026-10-14 and lists fixes for three CVEs in the PostgreSQL connection pooler, according to the [PgBouncer changelog](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/pgbouncer/pgbouncer/pgbouncer_1_26_1/NEWS.md). The [GitHub release](https://github.com/pgbouncer/pgbouncer/releases/tag/pgbouncer_1_26_1) was published at 08:28 UTC on October 14. The most serious by CVSS score, CVE-2026-107350, concerns SCRAM authentication and affects 1.17.0 through 1.26.0.

## What the Release Fixes

**CVE-2026-107350.** The changelog says PgBouncer 1.17.0 through 1.26.0 processed a second StartupMessage sent during SCRAM authentication when the client connected to a non-existent database. An attacker who knows the password of a user listed in `auth_file` could use this to log in as any other user that authenticates using SCRAM, including admins and backend superusers, per the [changelog](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/pgbouncer/pgbouncer/pgbouncer_1_26_1/NEWS.md). It requires SCRAM authentication to be used for both users, and the impersonated user can come from either `auth_file` or `auth_query`. The [GitHub Advisory Database entry](https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-qcxp-3cx5-3f3g) lists a CVSS 3.1 score of 8.8 (vector `CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:L/UI:N/S:U/C:H/I:H/A:H`) and CWE-287, Improper Authentication.

**CVE-2026-107349.** An unauthenticated client could make PgBouncer 1.20.0 through 1.26.0 spin forever on a CPU core, and thus stop serving all clients, by sending a startup `options` parameter containing an empty option name such as `-c=`, according to the [changelog](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/pgbouncer/pgbouncer/pgbouncer_1_26_1/NEWS.md). It is only exploitable when `ignore_startup_parameters` is non-empty but does not contain `options`. The [GitHub Advisory Database entry](https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-h8cj-p2h5-hm79) lists a CVSS 3.1 score of 7.5 (vector `CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:N/UI:N/S:U/C:N/I:N/A:H`) and CWE-400, Uncontrolled Resource Consumption.

**CVE-2026-107348.** An integer overflow in the packet buffer growth logic of versions 1.21.0 through 1.26.0 could cause PgBouncer to hang in an infinite loop when a client sent a packet header declaring a length above 2^31, per the [changelog](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/pgbouncer/pgbouncer/pgbouncer_1_26_1/NEWS.md). The changelog says this is only exploitable when `max_packet_size` is set to 2147483649 or higher, and that the default of 2147483647 is not affected. It also says the flaw has been reachable before authentication since 1.23.0, and that it is the same class of bug as CVE-2026-6668, but in a different buffer implementation. The [GitHub Advisory Database entry](https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-982p-g5h4-w372) lists a CVSS 3.1 score of 5.9 (vector `CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:H/PR:N/UI:N/S:U/C:N/I:N/A:H`) and CWE-190, Integer Overflow or Wraparound.

The scores and CWE identifiers come from GitHub's advisory database, not from the PgBouncer changelog, which gives no severity ratings. The advisory entries name no credited reporters, and neither does the changelog.

## A Configuration Fix in the Same Release

The one non-security entry changes `ignore_startup_parameters` so that it takes precedence over tracked parameters. According to the [changelog](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/pgbouncer/pgbouncer/pgbouncer_1_26_1/NEWS.md), `search_path` has been tracked by default since 1.26.0, which made `ignore_startup_parameters = search_path` silently have no effect. The changelog adds that various bugs were reported around tracking of `search_path` since that release and that "These bugs will be addressed in a later release." Adding `search_path` to `ignore_startup_parameters` now restores the 1.25 behaviour of ignoring it, it says.

## What We Don't Know

None of the sources cited here reports exploitation of the three CVEs. This article did not check the packaging status of 1.26.1 in Linux distributions. The Machine Herald [previously reported](/article/2026-05/11-pgbouncer-1252-patches-four-cves-including-a-pre-auth-scram-crash-that-hits-every-currently-shipping-debian-release) on a separate set of four PgBouncer CVEs fixed in 1.25.2 on May 8, 2026; the 1.26.1 fixes are a different set.
